subject: NimblePath switch economics & ops-risk outline
messages:
From: Evan Saito <evan.saito@nimbpath.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbpath.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring replacement — cost parity and transition support

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NimblePath leadership is interested in the cost/ops case for moving off our incumbent (AtlasAI) and onto Redwood for runtime inference. Two asks from procurement and engineering: 1) a concise price match/comparison that shows TCO breakpoints (token pricing, reserved capacity vs committed discount), and 2) a proposed migration incentive (credits, free onboarding days, or technical support) to offset migration risk.

Quick context: current annualized spend with AtlasAI is ~USD 1.2M with a blended per-token effective rate (including overage and reserved credits) they claim is ~0.00045/token for our workload. We have strict latency requirements (p95 < 250 ms) and use a mix of chat and embeddings.

Can you share a formal offer and a simple two-column comparison (AtlasAI vs Redwood) that calls out feature parity, cost ladders, and recommended ramp credits? Procurement is aiming to have an RFP decision by May 1.

Attached is our current contract summary for reference.

Cheers,
Evan

Attachment: nimblepath-current-contract-summary.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Saito <evan.saito@nimbpath.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement — cost parity and transition support

Evan — thanks for the clear context and the contract summary. We can absolutely put together a concise comparison and an incentive package aligned to your timeline. High level upfront so procurement has something to react to:

- Price-match framework: we can match AtlasAI's reported blended effective token rate for the first 6 months with a 6-month minimum commitment, subject to a usage ramp schedule. After the initial period, pricing transitions to our standard committed tier rates.
- Migration incentives: three options we typically propose (pick one or combine):
  1) Migration credit: USD 120k onboarding credit applied over first 3 billing cycles.
  2) Dedicated migration sprint: 10 engineering days (Redwood SEs) at no charge + technical-handoff checklist.
  3) Ramp discount: an additional 15% off committed tier pricing for months 4–6 to smooth unit economics.
- Operational guardrails: we will commit to a p95 latency SLO for your primary region and provide a fallback policy if latency or errors exceed thresholds during rollout.

Marcus and Kimberly — can you review the concession ranges and confirm floor rates and any operational notes (eg. egress, KV-cache warmup, dedicated pool sizing)? I’ll turn this into a short two-column comparison PDF and a formal offer (v1) to send Evan by EOD tomorrow.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: placeholder-internal-checklist.txt
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement — cost parity and transition support (internal)

Jordan / Kim — quick internal summary and recommended limits before we externalize: 

- Pricing floor: we should not go below an effective per-token floor of 0.00038 for standard chat workloads unless there is a committed reserved capacity contract that covers GPU ops. AtlasAI's 0.00045 effective was likely driven by a blended reserved discount plus some caching behavior; call that out explicitly in the comparison.
- Credits: USD 120k onboarding credit is fine, but cap it to one-time use versus recurring discounts. Offer can be structured as credits applied to invoices during months 1–3 and tied to a signed SOW.
- Technical support: 10 SE days is OK (we can do 5 remote + 5 onsite for an extra fee). Make the onsite contingent on a travel budget approval.
- Ops caveats to include in the doc: cache-warmup behavior (first 48–72 hrs token volume may be higher until prefixes stabilize), KV memory sizing differences vs AtlasAI, egress assumptions if they pull embeddings externally. Add line items for optional Dedicated pool sizing (N GPUs) with estimated throughput and cost.

Attach: ops-impact-analysis.pdf (high level) and technical-handoff-checklist.xlsx.

Limit concessions: total one-off value (credits + SE days) not to exceed 15% of first-year ACV without manager approval.

—Marcus
Senior Director, Product Ops
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Saito <evan.saito@nimbpath.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbpath.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood offer — NimblePath comparison and proposed migration package

Evan — thank you for the patience. Attached is a concise two-page comparison (AtlasAI vs Redwood) and our formal offer (v1). Key points up front:

1) Cost parity option (short term): Redwood will match the effective blended token economics you shared (0.00045/token) for the first 6 months under a 6-month minimum commitment. This is contingent on a signed MSA and a committed monthly usage ramp schedule we agree on in the SOW.

2) Migration package (choose a combination):
   • USD 120,000 onboarding credit applied across the first 3 invoices.
   • 10 SE days of technical migration support (5 remote + 5 onsite optional).
   • Ramp discount: additional 15% off committed tier pricing for months 4–6 if monthly usage targets are met.

3) Operational commitments: we will provide a dedicated rollout runbook, a technical-handoff checklist, and an SLO-backed latency target for your primary region. We will also include a brief ops-impact appendix that calls out KV cache warmup and expected short-term egress variability.

Attachments included: NimblePath-offer-v1.pdf, technical-handoff-checklist.xlsx, ops-impact-analysis.pdf

Next steps requested from you:
- Confirm which migration credits you want prioritized (credit vs extra SE days vs ramp discount).
- Provide top-20 queries and expected QPS at peak and steady state so we can size a dedicated pool if needed.
- Procurement timeline confirmation (you indicated May 1 for an RFP decision).

If this sounds reasonable I’ll ask Legal to start the MSA redline and have Finance build an ACV schedule for the committed tier. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the two-pager.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
